questions.stem: Which device normally chooses a next hop between IP networks?
questions.explanation: Routing connects IP networks; a hub repeats signals and a Layer 2 switch forwards frames within a VLAN.

questions.stem: Which function distinguishes an IPS from a passive IDS?
options: It can block detected malicious traffic inline
questions.explanation: An inline IPS can take preventive action. A passive detection system primarily observes and alerts.

questions.stem: What is the primary role of a wireless access point?
options: Bridge wireless clients onto a network
questions.explanation: An AP provides radio access and connects wireless stations with the wired infrastructure.

questions.stem: Why use a wireless LAN controller for many APs?
options: Give every AP a public address
questions.explanation: Controller management coordinates AP settings; physical connectivity and RF planning are still necessary.

questions.stem: Which two statements about Power over Ethernet are correct?
options: Electrical power can travel over Ethernet cabling
A switch has a finite power budget
It requires fiber instead of copper
questions.explanation: PoE can power compatible endpoints on Ethernet copper. The available switch power budget limits how many devices can be powered.

questions.stem: A PoE switch powers existing phones but cannot power one more AP. Cabling and AP compatibility check out. What should you inspect next?
questions.explanation: Each powered device consumes part of the switch power budget; a valid link does not guarantee power capacity.

questions.stem: Which medium is typically best for a long campus link of several kilometers?
options: Short multimode patch cable with arbitrary optics
questions.explanation: Single-mode fiber and matching optics support longer distances. Always verify the transceiver reach specifications.

questions.stem: Why is fiber useful between areas with strong electromagnetic interference?
options: It carries light rather than electrical signaling
questions.explanation: Optical signaling is resistant to electromagnetic interference; this is separate from encryption or topology control.

questions.stem: A copper interface accumulates CRC errors. Which two checks are most useful first?
questions.explanation: Damaged cabling and link-parameter problems can corrupt frames. CRC counters alone do not prove a single cause.

questions.stem: A half-duplex side reports late collisions while the opposite side is forced full duplex. What is the likely problem?
questions.explanation: The two ends disagree about collision handling. Use compatible negotiation or matching supported settings.

questions.stem: What does this interface state identify?
options: The interface is explicitly disabled in configuration
The interface has an OSPF mismatch
questions.explanation: Administratively down indicates shutdown configuration. Enable it with no shutdown and then verify the physical link.
questions.cli: GigabitEthernet0/1 is administratively down, line protocol is down

questions.stem: Which observation best fits this output?
options: The physical link is up, but the line protocol is not operational
The port was shut down administratively
questions.explanation: The first state describes the physical interface; line protocol describes its data-link operation. More investigation is needed.
questions.cli: Serial0/0/0 is up, line protocol is down

questions.stem: A collapsed-core campus combines which traditional layers?
questions.explanation: A two-tier design commonly combines distribution and core functions while retaining the access layer.

questions.stem: In a typical spine-leaf fabric, how do leaf switches connect?
options: Each leaf connects to every spine
Each leaf connects only to its nearest leaf
A single daisy chain connects every switch
questions.explanation: All-to-all leaf-to-spine connectivity creates predictable paths through the fabric.

questions.stem: What does a WAN primarily interconnect?
options: Only virtual machines in one host
questions.explanation: WAN technologies connect sites beyond an individual local-area network.

questions.stem: Which two characteristics are common in SOHO networks?
options: A small number of users and devices
An integrated router with wireless access
questions.explanation: SOHO networks serve small offices or homes and often combine routing, switching and wireless functions. They still need appropriate security.

questions.stem: What is a hypervisor used for?
options: Running multiple virtual machines on a host
Replacing all operating systems with JSON
questions.explanation: A hypervisor allocates host resources to VMs, each of which can have its own guest operating system.

questions.stem: Which two statements distinguish containers and full virtual machines?
options: Containers commonly share a host OS kernel
A virtual machine can have its own guest operating system
Every container needs a dedicated physical server
Every VM must share its guest kernel with the host
questions.explanation: Containers package isolated applications around a shared kernel. Full VMs run guest OS environments managed by a hypervisor.

questions.stem: Why might two tenants both use 10.0.0.0/24 on one router?
options: Separate VRFs maintain separate routing tables
A VLAN tag changes the IP address
questions.explanation: VRFs separate routing contexts, allowing overlapping address spaces when interfaces are assigned appropriately.

questions.stem: Which address does a switch learn from an arriving Ethernet frame?
questions.explanation: Learning associates the source MAC with the ingress port and VLAN. Destination MAC is used for the forwarding lookup.

questions.stem: A switch has no entry for a unicast destination. What happens within that VLAN?
options: It floods eligible ports except the ingress port
It asks DNS for a port
questions.explanation: Unknown unicast flooding is confined to the VLAN and eligible forwarding ports.

questions.stem: A frame arrives on the same port recorded for its destination MAC. What does a switch normally do?
options: Filter the frame instead of forwarding it back
questions.explanation: The destination is reachable through the incoming segment, so sending the frame back through that port is unnecessary.

questions.stem: Which address is the Ethernet broadcast address?
questions.explanation: All 48 destination MAC bits are set for an Ethernet broadcast. The other multicast examples are IP addresses.

questions.stem: Why do dynamic MAC entries age out?
questions.explanation: Aging removes entries that have not been refreshed, helping the switch adapt when endpoints move or disappear.

questions.stem: Which two functions are provided by TCP?
questions.explanation: TCP uses sequence numbers and acknowledgments for reliable ordered delivery. Encryption requires another mechanism.

questions.stem: Why might real-time voice use UDP?
options: It avoids TCP retransmission delays and connection overhead
questions.explanation: Delay-sensitive applications can prefer timely delivery over retransmission; loss and jitter still require design attention.

questions.stem: What identifies an application conversation at the transport layer?
questions.explanation: TCP and UDP ports distinguish application endpoints alongside IP addresses and the transport protocol.

questions.stem: What changes when an IPv4 packet crosses a router without NAT?
options: The Layer 2 header is replaced and TTL decreases
Both endpoint IP addresses must change
questions.explanation: Routing re-encapsulates the packet for the next link and decrements TTL. Endpoint addresses remain unchanged without translation.

questions.stem: A host sends to a remote IPv4 subnet. Which MAC address does it normally use as the Ethernet destination?
questions.explanation: The gateway is the local next hop. ARP resolves that local address; remote MAC addresses do not traverse routers.

questions.stem: What information does ARP resolve for a local IPv4 neighbor?
questions.explanation: ARP locates the local link-layer destination needed to send an IPv4 packet on Ethernet.

questions.stem: Which address belongs to an RFC 1918 private range?
questions.explanation: The private 172 range extends from 172.16.0.0 through 172.31.255.255; the surrounding 172 addresses are not all private.

questions.stem: Which two are private IPv4 prefixes?
questions.explanation: RFC 1918 reserves 10/8, 172.16/12 and 192.168/16. Link-local 169.254/16 is a different category.

questions.stem: A Windows client self-assigns 169.254.10.20/16 instead of its normal LAN address. What should you investigate?
options: Whether the client is the STP root
questions.explanation: An IPv4 link-local address commonly indicates the client did not obtain a DHCP lease; it does not identify the precise cause.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of a subnet mask?
questions.explanation: The mask defines the prefix boundary used to determine whether a destination is on-link.

questions.stem: Why allocate the largest subnet requirements first in VLSM planning?
options: To preserve aligned blocks large enough for the biggest networks
questions.explanation: Allocating large aligned blocks first reduces fragmentation of the available address space.

questions.stem: A host can ping its own subnet but cannot reach any remote subnet. Which host setting is most directly relevant?
questions.explanation: Off-link traffic needs a next-hop gateway. Local connectivity does not prove that gateway configuration is correct.

questions.stem: Which Windows command shows the configured IPv4 address, mask, gateway and DNS servers?
questions.explanation: ipconfig /all displays detailed adapter configuration on Windows.

questions.stem: Which Linux command displays interface IP addresses?
questions.explanation: The ip utility provides Linux interface and routing information; ip address show lists addresses.

questions.stem: Why can a host with the wrong mask fail only for some destinations?
options: It may incorrectly decide a remote destination is on-link
All incorrect masks immediately disable the link
questions.explanation: A host that treats a remote address as local may ARP for it instead of using the gateway.

questions.stem: How long is an IPv6 address?
questions.explanation: IPv6 has 128 address bits. A common LAN prefix is /64, but that is not the full address length.

questions.stem: Which prefix identifies IPv6 link-local addresses?
questions.explanation: Link-local addresses are limited to a link; global unicast, multicast and unique local use other prefixes.

questions.stem: Which prefix is reserved for IPv6 unique local addressing?
questions.explanation: Unique local addresses are intended for local use; locally assigned examples commonly start with FD.

questions.stem: What is IPv6 anycast?
options: The same unicast address on multiple nodes, reached through routing to one instance
One packet delivered to every node
An address usable only on loopbacks
questions.explanation: Anycast relies on routing to deliver to a selected, typically topologically nearest, instance.

questions.stem: What replaces IPv4-style broadcasts in IPv6 for many discovery functions?
questions.explanation: IPv6 does not define broadcast addressing; multicast serves group communication needs.

questions.stem: What does modified EUI-64 do to a 48-bit MAC when constructing an interface ID?
options: Insert FFFE and invert the universal/local bit
questions.explanation: The identifier becomes 64 bits by insertion, and the U/L bit is toggled. Other IPv6 interface-ID methods also exist.

questions.stem: Which IPv6 address represents loopback?
questions.explanation: Loopback identifies the local host. The all-zero address :: is the unspecified address.

questions.stem: How many times may :: appear in one compressed IPv6 address?
questions.explanation: A single omitted run has an unambiguous length. Multiple :: runs would make reconstruction ambiguous.

questions.stem: An IPv6 static route uses a link-local next hop on Ethernet. What additional information is needed?
questions.explanation: A link-local address is scoped to its link, so the router needs an interface to identify that link.

questions.stem: Which global command enables IPv6 packet forwarding on Cisco IOS routers?
questions.explanation: An interface IPv6 address alone is not the global IPv6 forwarding switch; ipv6 unicast-routing enables forwarding.

questions.stem: Which protocol supports IPv6 neighbor discovery?
questions.explanation: Neighbor Discovery uses ICMPv6 messages, including neighbor and router solicitations and advertisements.

questions.stem: Which is the fully expanded form of 2001:db8:1::a?
questions.explanation: Expand to eight groups of four hexadecimal digits, preserving the nonzero group positions.

questions.stem: Which 2.4 GHz channels are a common nonoverlapping 20 MHz plan in the US?
questions.explanation: The separation between these channels avoids the substantial overlap of adjacent 2.4 GHz channels.

questions.stem: What is an SSID?
questions.explanation: Clients select wireless networks by SSID; the name itself does not provide security.

questions.stem: Why can increasing channel width reduce usable channel reuse?
questions.explanation: Greater width may increase potential throughput but leaves fewer nonoverlapping choices in a limited band.

questions.stem: Nearby APs on overlapping 2.4 GHz channels have poor throughput. What change is most appropriate to evaluate?
options: A nonoverlapping channel plan and appropriate transmit power
Put every AP at maximum power
Change all clients to static DNS
questions.explanation: RF planning addresses interference; excessive power or overlapping channels can make performance worse.

questions.stem: With similar power and conditions, why may 2.4 GHz reach farther indoors than 5 GHz?
options: Lower-frequency signals generally experience less propagation loss
questions.explanation: Propagation depends on frequency and obstacles. Real coverage also depends on power, antennas and the building.

questions.stem: What does public cloud computing typically allow an organization to do?
options: Consume provider-hosted computing resources on demand
questions.explanation: Cloud services offer remotely hosted capacity; responsibilities and network latency still need consideration.

questions.stem: A switch learns the same MAC on a new port in the same VLAN. What normally changes?
options: The MAC table points to the new ingress port
The endpoint must get a new IP
questions.explanation: Dynamic learning updates the location of the source MAC. Rapid repeated moves may warrant investigation.

questions.stem: Which Ethernet mode permits simultaneous sending and receiving without collisions?
questions.explanation: Full-duplex point-to-point Ethernet has independent transmit and receive operation; normal collisions should not occur.

questions.stem: How does a SLAAC host learn the network prefix?
questions.explanation: Router Advertisements carry prefix information and router availability. SLAAC does not require a DHCPv6 address assignment.

questions.stem: Which two statements about VLANs are correct?
options: Each VLAN forms a separate broadcast domain
Routing is needed for normal communication between different VLAN subnets
Every VLAN needs its own physical switch
A trunk can carry only one VLAN
questions.explanation: A VLAN separates Layer 2 broadcast scope. Layer 3 forwarding connects IP subnets associated with different VLANs.

questions.stem: What is the default access VLAN on a typical Cisco switch?
questions.explanation: Access interfaces normally start in VLAN 1 until configured otherwise.

questions.stem: Two PCs are in different VLANs. What is needed for normal IP communication between them?
questions.explanation: Layer 2 VLAN separation requires a router or Layer 3 switch for inter-VLAN forwarding.

questions.stem: Which interface command assigns an access port to VLAN 20?
questions.explanation: The access VLAN setting selects the data VLAN for an access port; trunk native VLAN is a different setting.

questions.stem: A PC connects through an IP phone. Which arrangement is commonly supported?
options: Separate data access VLAN and tagged voice VLAN on the switch port
Exactly one mandatory shared IP subnet
Two OSPF areas on the phone
No VLAN tagging for any phone traffic
questions.explanation: The phone can tag voice traffic while the attached PC uses the data access VLAN.

questions.stem: Which standard tags Ethernet frames with VLAN information on trunks?
questions.explanation: 802.1Q identifies VLAN membership across a trunk. The other standards concern PoE, access control and wireless.

questions.stem: By default, how is native VLAN traffic sent on an 802.1Q trunk?
questions.explanation: Native traffic is normally untagged unless native VLAN tagging has been explicitly configured.

questions.stem: A trunk has native VLAN 10 on one end and 20 on the other. What risk does this create?
options: Untagged traffic can enter different VLANs at opposite ends
questions.explanation: Each end classifies untagged frames into its own native VLAN, producing inconsistent VLAN membership.

questions.stem: VLAN 30 exists on both switches but cannot cross this link. What configuration directly explains it?
options: VLAN 30 is absent from the allowed list
VLAN 30 must be the native VLAN
The interface is necessarily shut down
The trunk uses the wrong routing protocol
questions.explanation: A VLAN must be allowed on the trunk to carry its traffic; existence in the VLAN database is insufficient.
questions.cli:
Port      Mode  Encapsulation Status    Native vlan
Gi0/1     on    802.1q        trunking  1
Port      Vlans allowed on trunk
Gi0/1     10,20

questions.stem: Which command adds VLAN 30 while retaining existing trunk allowances?
questions.explanation: The add keyword modifies the allowed set. Omitting it replaces the set with the specified list.

questions.stem: Two ports are both dynamic auto and remain access ports. What explains this?
options: Neither side actively initiates trunk negotiation
questions.explanation: Two passive DTP auto ports do not negotiate a trunk. Explicit trunk configuration removes this ambiguity.

questions.stem: Which command directly reports operational trunk links and allowed VLAN lists?
questions.explanation: Trunk output shows operational state and VLAN forwarding information.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of encapsulation dot1Q 40 on a router subinterface?
options: Associate that subinterface with VLAN 40 traffic
questions.explanation: Router-on-a-stick subinterfaces use VLAN encapsulation and an IP address to route for the associated VLAN.

questions.stem: A multilayer switch has correctly addressed SVIs but does not route between VLANs. What global setting should you verify?
questions.explanation: SVIs provide Layer 3 interfaces; the switch also needs routing enabled to forward between them.

questions.stem: Which range is normally described as normal-range VLAN IDs?
questions.explanation: Normal range includes reserved legacy VLANs 1002–1005. Not all IDs in the range are available for ordinary user assignment.

questions.stem: An SVI is administratively enabled but down. Which condition should you verify?
options: The VLAN exists and has an active eligible forwarding port
The SVI has a public address
DNS is enabled on every port
The VLAN number equals the mask length
questions.explanation: SVI line state commonly depends on VLAN activity and autostate rules; platform details can vary.

questions.stem: What problem does STP prevent in redundant Layer 2 topologies?
questions.explanation: STP blocks selected redundant paths to create a loop-free forwarding topology.

questions.stem: Which bridge becomes the STP root?
options: The bridge with the lowest bridge ID
questions.explanation: Bridge ID compares priority, including system-ID extension, and then MAC address.

questions.stem: Two switches have equal STP priority in one VLAN. Which becomes root?
options: The one with the lower MAC address
The one with the higher MAC address
The one with a higher hostname alphabetically
questions.explanation: MAC address breaks a bridge-ID tie when the priority components are equal.

questions.stem: What is a root port on a nonroot switch?
options: Its selected best path toward the root bridge
A port only on the root bridge
questions.explanation: A nonroot bridge selects one root port per spanning-tree instance based on path and tie-break criteria.

questions.stem: What is a designated port on a segment?
options: The selected port offering that segment the best path to the root
questions.explanation: The designated port is the forwarding representative for that segment in the STP topology.

questions.stem: Which three are RSTP port states?
questions.explanation: RSTP consolidates legacy disabled, blocking and listening behavior into discarding, while retaining learning and forwarding.

questions.stem: Does an RSTP learning port forward user frames?
options: No, but it can learn source MAC addresses
Only frames from the root router
questions.explanation: Learning populates MAC information before the port begins user-data forwarding.

questions.stem: What does PortFast change on an appropriate edge port?
options: It allows rapid transition to forwarding
It disables all STP processing permanently
It elects the local switch as root
questions.explanation: PortFast is intended for edge connections. It avoids normal startup delay but is not a substitute for loop protection.

questions.stem: A PortFast edge port with BPDU guard becomes error-disabled after a switch is connected. Why?
options: Its OSPF cost was too high
questions.explanation: BPDU guard protects an edge assumption by disabling a port that receives a BPDU.

questions.stem: Which STP feature prevents a downstream switch from becoming root through a protected port?
questions.explanation: Root guard places the port into a root-inconsistent state if superior BPDUs would make it a root path.

questions.stem: Which feature helps stop a blocked port from forwarding when expected BPDUs disappear?
questions.explanation: Loop guard can hold the affected port in a loop-inconsistent condition instead of allowing an unsafe transition.

questions.stem: Why is interface-level BPDU filtering dangerous on an interswitch link?
options: It guarantees a better root election
questions.explanation: Suppressing BPDUs can defeat STP's loop prevention. BPDU filtering behavior depends on how it is configured.

questions.stem: What does this output tell you about Gi0/2?
options: It is an alternate path currently discarding user traffic
questions.explanation: Alternate ports provide a redundant path. BLK output corresponds to nonforwarding behavior.
questions.cli:
Interface  Role Sts Cost
Gi0/1      Root FWD 4
Gi0/2      Altn BLK 4

questions.stem: What does Rapid PVST+ maintain?
options: A separate rapid spanning-tree instance per VLAN
One shared IP routing table for all routers
A single mandatory instance for every VLAN
questions.explanation: Per-VLAN instances allow distinct root and path choices across VLANs.

questions.stem: What does EtherChannel provide?
options: Multiple physical links acting as one logical link
questions.explanation: Bundling provides aggregate capacity and redundancy while presenting a logical port-channel.

questions.stem: Which LACP mode actively sends negotiation messages?
questions.explanation: Active initiates LACP negotiation. Auto and desirable belong to PAgP rather than LACP.

questions.stem: Which two LACP pairings can form a channel when other parameters match?
questions.explanation: LACP requires at least one active participant. Active/active and active/passive can negotiate; auto and desirable are PAgP modes.

questions.stem: Both peers use LACP passive and no channel forms. What is a minimal fix?
options: Change one native VLAN to a different value
Remove the port-channel interface address only
questions.explanation: One active peer initiates the LACP exchange while the other can remain passive.

questions.stem: Which two settings should be consistent among Layer 2 channel members?
questions.explanation: Members must be compatible at Layer 2. Different physical numbers or device hostnames do not prevent bundling.

questions.stem: What does the P flag identify for these member interfaces?
options: They are bundled in the port-channel
questions.explanation: P indicates bundled membership; SU indicates a Layer 2 channel in use.
questions.cli:
Group Port-channel Protocol Ports
1     Po1(SU)      LACP     Gi0/1(P) Gi0/2(P)

questions.stem: Where should the IP address of a Layer 3 EtherChannel be configured?
options: Separately using the same IP on every member
questions.explanation: The bundle is one logical Layer 3 interface. Physical members should be configured compatibly as routed ports.

questions.stem: Why does one TCP flow often fail to use the sum of all EtherChannel member speeds?
options: A hash normally assigns that flow to one member
LACP transmits all data at 1 Mbps
questions.explanation: Aggregation distributes multiple flows. One flow generally remains on one link to preserve ordering.

questions.stem: A two-link channel remains up after one member fails. What changes?
options: The channel must lose its IP address
questions.explanation: Remaining members can continue forwarding, but fewer physical links reduce available bandwidth.

questions.stem: Which discovery protocol is an IEEE standard?
questions.explanation: LLDP is standardized as IEEE 802.1AB; CDP is Cisco's discovery protocol.

questions.stem: Which command reveals directly connected Cisco neighbors and their port IDs?
questions.explanation: CDP reports local links, device IDs, capabilities and remote port IDs where enabled.

questions.stem: Can CDP discover a device several routers away through routed forwarding?
options: No, it discovers directly connected neighbors
Only if every router is DR
questions.explanation: CDP is a link-local discovery mechanism; ordinary routing does not propagate its advertisements.

questions.stem: Which management protocol encrypts a CLI session?
questions.explanation: SSH protects the management session. Telnet sends session content without equivalent encryption.

questions.stem: Which access method is useful when remote IP connectivity is broken?
options: HTTPS to the failed IP path
SNMP over the same failed route
questions.explanation: A local console connection does not require normal network-layer connectivity to the device.

questions.stem: Which web-management option provides transport encryption?
questions.explanation: HTTPS uses TLS to protect the browser-to-device session, subject to correct certificate validation.

questions.stem: Which protocol carries control between a lightweight AP and its WLC?
questions.explanation: CAPWAP provides controller/AP communication; centrally switched WLAN data can also be tunneled.

questions.stem: What is a key FlexConnect capability?
options: Local switching of selected client traffic at a branch
Mandatory tunneling of all traffic in every configuration
Replacing the branch router with DNS
questions.explanation: FlexConnect can switch WLAN traffic locally, depending on policy and configuration.

questions.stem: What does an AP in monitor mode primarily do?
options: Scan and monitor wireless conditions rather than serve ordinary clients
questions.explanation: Monitor mode dedicates the AP to monitoring tasks instead of normal client service.

questions.stem: Clients associate to a WLAN but obtain addresses from the wrong subnet. Which mapping should you inspect?
questions.explanation: The WLAN's mapped VLAN determines the Layer 2 segment and therefore its expected DHCP scope.

questions.stem: Why might a FlexConnect AP need a trunk uplink?
options: To locally switch multiple client VLANs
Because all AP links must carry every VLAN
Because CAPWAP cannot cross routed networks
questions.explanation: Local switching across several VLANs requires appropriate tagging and VLAN allowance on the AP uplink.

questions.stem: A newly configured WLAN is not visible to clients. Which two GUI settings are relevant first?
questions.explanation: An administratively disabled WLAN or hidden SSID can explain visibility behavior; radio and AP policy also matter.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of a voice QoS profile on a WLAN?
options: Give suitable treatment to delay-sensitive voice traffic
questions.explanation: QoS classifies and prioritizes traffic; it cannot create capacity or guarantee an interference-free radio link.

questions.stem: What does a WLC link aggregation group combine?
options: Multiple wired uplinks into a logical bundle
Multiple client IPs into one DHCP lease
Several RF bands into one channel
questions.explanation: LAG concerns the wired uplinks. Supported negotiation and configuration details depend on controller platform.

questions.stem: An access PC in VLAN 10 can reach a same-switch peer but not a peer in VLAN 10 on another switch. Which is the best next check?
options: VLAN 10 forwarding on the interswitch trunk
Whether VLAN 10 has a public subnet
The OSPF DR priority on the PC
questions.explanation: Local success narrows the failure toward the interswitch path, including allowed VLANs and spanning-tree state.

questions.stem: What does this output most directly identify?
options: SW2 connects to local Gi0/1 using its Gi0/24
SW2 is definitely the root bridge
Gi0/1 has an IP address of 24
questions.explanation: Discovery neighbor output maps local and remote physical interfaces; it does not establish routing or STP roles.
questions.cli:
Device ID  Local Intf  Capability  Port ID
SW2        Gi0/1       S I         Gi0/24

questions.stem: A router subinterface uses VLAN 50 but the switch trunk allows only 10 and 20. What change is required for VLAN 50 clients?
options: Allow VLAN 50 on the trunk and verify that VLAN is active
Make the router an LACP passive peer
Change all clients to loopback addresses
questions.explanation: The tagged frames must reach the router subinterface through an allowed, active VLAN.

questions.stem: What happens to a root-guard port when superior BPDUs stop arriving and conditions recover?
options: It can automatically leave the root-inconsistent state
questions.explanation: Root guard blocks an undesirable root path while the condition exists; recovery is automatic when the condition clears.

questions.stem: Channel members have different native VLAN settings. What should you do first?
options: Set all OSPF priorities to zero
questions.explanation: Inconsistent VLAN settings can prevent a valid bundle and cause suspended members or mismatched behavior.

questions.stem: What does a router primarily examine to forward an ordinary unicast IP packet?
questions.explanation: The forwarding lookup matches the destination against installed routes.

questions.stem: Which installed route wins when several prefixes match a packet?
options: The route with the longest matching prefix
questions.explanation: Prefix specificity governs forwarding. Administrative distance selects between candidate sources for the same prefix during route installation.

questions.stem: An OSPF /24 and a static /16 are installed. A destination matches both. Which is used?
options: Whichever has the lower next-hop IP
questions.explanation: The /24 matches more destination bits. The static route's lower administrative distance does not override specificity.

questions.stem: What is administrative distance used to compare?
options: Preference of route sources for the same prefix
questions.explanation: AD is a local route-source preference. It is not a universal measure of path quality.

questions.stem: What do the bracketed numbers mean?
questions.explanation: Cisco route output uses [administrative distance/metric].

questions.stem: What route code identifies a directly connected network?
questions.explanation: C marks the connected subnet. L marks a local host route for an interface's own address.

questions.stem: Why is there an L /32 route for 192.168.1.1?
options: It identifies the router's own IPv4 interface address
It represents every host on the LAN
It is a learned default route
questions.explanation: The local host route directs packets addressed to the router itself for local processing.
questions.cli:
C 192.168.1.0/24 is directly connected, Gi0/0
L 192.168.1.1/32 is directly connected, Gi0/0

questions.stem: No installed route matches a destination, and there is no default. What does the router normally do?
options: Drop the packet, possibly generating ICMP unreachable
Ask DNS to choose a route
Send it to the lowest MAC address
questions.explanation: A router needs a matching forwarding entry. It does not use Layer 2 flooding to discover an IP path.

questions.stem: What is the IPv4 default route prefix?
questions.explanation: A zero-length prefix matches every IPv4 address and is used when no more-specific route applies.

questions.stem: Which has the lowest default administrative distance?
questions.explanation: Connected routes have AD 0; ordinary static routes have AD 1 and OSPF has AD 110.

questions.stem: Can you directly compare an OSPF cost of 10 to a RIP metric of 2 to choose a protocol?
options: No; the metrics have different meanings
questions.explanation: Different protocols calculate metrics differently. Route-source selection uses administrative distance for an identical prefix.

questions.stem: Two equal-cost OSPF routes to the same prefix are installed. What can the router do?
options: Convert the prefix to a host route
questions.explanation: Supported ECMP behavior allows traffic distribution across equal eligible next hops; distribution need not alternate every packet.

questions.stem: Which command installs an IPv4 default route through 192.0.2.1?
questions.explanation: The destination and mask are both zero for an IPv4 default static route.

questions.stem: Which route targets only 10.1.2.3?
questions.explanation: A /32 route matches one IPv4 address, while shorter prefixes cover broader networks.

questions.stem: What makes a static route floating?
options: An administrative distance above the preferred route's distance
questions.explanation: It stays out of the active table while the preferred route for the same prefix remains available.

questions.stem: Will this backup route replace a working default-AD OSPF route to the same /24?
options: No; its AD 120 is higher than OSPF's 110
No; static routes cannot back up OSPF
questions.explanation: The elevated distance makes the static route a backup for the identical prefix.

questions.stem: A next-hop-only static route is configured but absent from the routing table. What should you check?
options: Whether the next hop can be resolved through a usable route
Whether the console is logged in
questions.explanation: A configured route may be ineligible if its next hop cannot be resolved. Configuration presence does not guarantee installation.

questions.stem: Which command installs an IPv6 default through global next hop 2001:db8:1::1?
questions.explanation: IPv6 uses prefix notation; ::/0 is the default destination.

questions.stem: What prefix length identifies an IPv6 host route?
questions.explanation: A host route matches all 128 bits of one IPv6 address.

questions.stem: Why can a forward static route alone be insufficient for ping?
options: A usable return path is also needed
Ping works only inside one VLAN
questions.explanation: The request and reply both need routing. A valid outward path does not establish return reachability.

questions.stem: A router can ping its WAN peer but not a remote LAN. What should you verify next?
options: Routes to the remote LAN and the return path
questions.explanation: Reaching the adjacent peer confirms the local link, not the full path to the remote subnet.

questions.stem: What type of routing protocol is OSPF?
questions.explanation: OSPF distributes link-state information within an autonomous system and calculates shortest paths.

questions.stem: Which algorithm does OSPF use to calculate paths?
questions.explanation: SPF builds shortest paths from the link-state database using OSPF costs.

questions.stem: Must OSPF process IDs match on neighboring Cisco routers?
options: No; the process ID is locally significant
Only when the router IDs match
questions.explanation: Neighbors must agree on relevant link parameters, but their local process numbers may differ.

questions.stem: Which OSPF area is the backbone area?
options: The area with the largest router ID
questions.explanation: Area 0 is the OSPF backbone. Single-area CCNA practice commonly uses it.

questions.stem: What does the OSPF network command select on IOS?
options: Local interfaces whose addresses match its address and wildcard
Only remote destination networks to install
questions.explanation: The command enables OSPF on matching local interfaces and assigns them to the specified area.

questions.stem: Which interface address matches this network statement?
questions.explanation: A zero wildcard bit must match; 0.0.0.255 permits any final octet within 10.1.2.0/24.

questions.stem: What is the format of an OSPF router ID?
options: A 32-bit value displayed like an IPv4 address
questions.explanation: Router IDs identify OSPF routers. The ID need not itself be a currently reachable interface address.

questions.stem: What takes precedence in OSPF router-ID selection?
questions.explanation: A manually configured ID has precedence. Otherwise IOS considers eligible loopback and other interface IPv4 addresses.

questions.stem: Without a manual ID, which is preferred when loopbacks exist at OSPF initialization?
options: The highest eligible loopback IPv4 address
The VLAN with the most hosts
questions.explanation: Loopback selection precedes nonloopback interface selection in the usual IOS router-ID process.

questions.stem: Two routers use the same OSPF router ID. What should you do?
options: Assign unique IDs and restart the relevant process when appropriate
questions.explanation: Duplicate router IDs undermine identification and topology information; plan process changes to avoid unintended disruption.

questions.stem: Which IP protocol number does OSPFv2 use?
questions.explanation: OSPFv2 runs directly over IP protocol 89; it does not use a TCP or UDP port.

questions.stem: Which multicast address is used for AllSPFRouters in OSPFv2?
questions.explanation: 224.0.0.5 identifies all OSPF routers on the link; .6 targets designated routers.

questions.stem: Which two link settings must normally agree for a working OSPFv2 adjacency?
questions.explanation: Area and timers are compatibility checks. Other checks include authentication and relevant network parameters.

questions.stem: R1 uses hello/dead 10/40 and R2 uses 5/20 on one Ethernet segment. What is the direct issue?
questions.explanation: Neighbors reject incompatible hello timing; configure matching timers and verify again.

questions.stem: What does FULL/DR describe in show ip ospf neighbor?
options: A fully adjacent neighbor that is the DR
The local router must be DR
questions.explanation: The suffix reports the neighbor's role, while FULL reports database synchronization status.

questions.stem: Two DROTHER routers on a healthy broadcast segment remain 2-WAY with each other. Is that necessarily a fault?
options: No; they normally form full adjacencies with the DR and BDR
Yes; every pair must always be FULL
No; they are not discovering each other
questions.explanation: DROTHER-to-DROTHER 2-WAY is expected in the broadcast adjacency model.

questions.stem: Neighbors remain in EXSTART/EXCHANGE. Which mismatch is a classic candidate to inspect?
questions.explanation: Database description exchange can fail with an MTU mismatch. The state suggests a check, not an exclusive diagnosis.

questions.stem: What does passive-interface do for an OSPF-enabled LAN?
options: Suppress neighbor formation while permitting advertisement of the connected prefix
Remove every route from the LAN
Make the LAN a different OSPF area
questions.explanation: A passive interface does not exchange OSPF hellos but its network can still be included in OSPF advertisements.

questions.stem: No OSPF hellos leave a correctly addressed link to another router. It is configured passive. What change is needed?
options: Remove passive status on that adjacency-facing interface
questions.explanation: Passive operation intentionally prevents neighbor formation. Keep passive status on endpoint-only LANs where appropriate.

questions.stem: What determines OSPF interface cost by default on Cisco IOS?
options: Reference bandwidth divided by interface bandwidth, with a minimum cost of 1
questions.explanation: Cost models bandwidth rather than delay or hop count; manual cost configuration can override the calculation.

questions.stem: Why adjust OSPF reference bandwidth in a high-speed network?
options: To distinguish link speeds that otherwise all have cost 1
questions.explanation: A low reference bandwidth collapses multiple high-speed links to the minimum cost. Use consistent planning across routers.

questions.stem: Is a DR elected on an OSPF point-to-point network type?
questions.explanation: Point-to-point OSPF does not require the broadcast segment DR/BDR model.

questions.stem: At a fresh broadcast election, which criterion is compared before router ID?
questions.explanation: The highest eligible priority wins; router ID breaks a priority tie.

questions.stem: What does ip ospf priority 0 do on a broadcast interface?
options: Makes it ineligible to become DR or BDR
questions.explanation: Priority zero excludes the router from DR/BDR election on that interface while allowing neighbor participation.

questions.stem: A higher-priority router joins a stable broadcast segment with a DR. Does it automatically replace that DR?
options: No; the election is normally nonpreemptive
Only if its hostname is shorter
Only if it has a static route
questions.explanation: An existing functioning DR is not displaced merely by a new higher-priority participant.

questions.stem: Which command is most direct for checking current OSPF adjacency states?
questions.explanation: Neighbor output reports IDs, states and associated interfaces; routing output alone does not show every adjacency detail.

questions.stem: What problem do first-hop redundancy protocols address?
options: Failure of a host's default gateway device
questions.explanation: A shared virtual gateway can remain available through another router when one gateway fails.

questions.stem: Which address should a host normally use with HSRP gateway redundancy?
options: Only the standby router's physical IP
questions.explanation: Using the virtual address allows gateway ownership to move without reconfiguring each host.

questions.stem: Which roles does an HSRP group use?
questions.explanation: The active router forwards for the virtual gateway; standby is ready to take over.

questions.stem: Does FHRP by itself create routes to all remote networks?
options: No; each gateway still needs appropriate routing
Only if the virtual IP is public
questions.explanation: Gateway redundancy preserves the first hop. Upstream connectivity and route availability must also be designed.

questions.stem: Traceroute stops after the first hop. Which conclusion is justified?
options: Further investigation is needed; filtering or a path problem could explain it
The second router is definitely powered off
questions.explanation: Missing ICMP responses do not uniquely locate a failure; some devices filter or rate-limit traceroute responses.

questions.stem: What does the asterisk in S* usually indicate?
questions.explanation: The code S identifies static and the asterisk marks candidate-default status.

questions.stem: Why specify both exit interface and next hop for an Ethernet static route when appropriate?
options: It identifies both the egress link and the adjacent next hop
It creates a routing protocol adjacency
questions.explanation: A fully specified route avoids treating every remote destination as directly attached on a multiaccess link.

questions.stem: What is this command doing?
options: Enabling OSPF process 1 in area 0 on this interface
questions.explanation: Interface-level OSPF activation selects the process and area without needing a matching network statement.
questions.cli:
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
 ip ospf 1 area 0

questions.stem: What is inside source NAT used to change?
options: Source addressing of traffic from the inside network
questions.explanation: Inside source translation maps inside addresses to the addresses used toward the outside.

questions.stem: Which term describes an inside host's address as used on its local network?
questions.explanation: Inside local identifies the internal address before inside-source translation.

questions.stem: What distinguishes static NAT from ordinary dynamic pool NAT?
options: Static NAT provides a configured fixed address mapping
Static NAT requires every session to use one port
Static NAT is a routing protocol
questions.explanation: Static NAT maps a specific inside local address to a specific inside global address; pool allocation is dynamic.

questions.stem: Why does PAT allow many inside hosts to share one global IPv4 address?
options: It distinguishes translations using transport identifiers such as ports
It assigns the same MAC to every host
It converts all traffic to broadcast
questions.explanation: Address-and-port translation separates flows sharing one global address.

questions.stem: What is the inside global address here?
questions.explanation: The inside global column shows the translated address visible toward the outside.
questions.cli:
Pro Inside global       Inside local      Outside local       Outside global
tcp 203.0.113.5:40001    10.1.1.10:51500    198.51.100.20:443   198.51.100.20:443

questions.stem: What does overload add to this configuration?
questions.explanation: The overload keyword permits multiple translations to share the selected inside global address through ports.
questions.cli: ip nat inside source list 10 interface GigabitEthernet0/1 overload

questions.stem: A pool has five addresses and uses dynamic NAT without overload. A sixth simultaneous inside host cannot get a mapping. Why?
options: The translation pool may be exhausted
questions.explanation: Without overload, ordinary dynamic address translations consume distinct global addresses.

questions.stem: A router has a valid NAT rule but no translations after traffic. Which two items should you inspect?
options: Whether traffic matches the NAT selection ACL
questions.explanation: NAT requires correct interface roles and a matching rule. Routing and the actual traffic path also matter.

questions.stem: Which command shows current NAT mappings?
questions.explanation: Translations show active address and, for PAT, port mappings.

questions.stem: Which order describes initial DHCPv4 address acquisition?
questions.explanation: The client discovers servers, receives an offer, requests a lease and receives acknowledgment.

questions.stem: Which UDP ports are used by DHCPv4 server and client?
questions.explanation: DHCPv4 uses UDP 67 on the server and UDP 68 on the client.

questions.stem: Why is DHCP relay needed for a server on another subnet?
options: Initial client broadcasts are not normally routed
DHCP cannot use any IP packets
All clients must be directly cabled to the server
questions.explanation: The relay conveys requests to a remote server and supplies subnet context for address selection.

questions.stem: Where is ip helper-address typically configured for client DHCP broadcasts?
options: On the Layer 3 interface facing the clients
Only on a Layer 2 access port
questions.explanation: The relay must receive the local client broadcast to forward it toward the DHCP server.

questions.stem: Which interface command makes a Cisco router obtain an IPv4 address by DHCP?
questions.explanation: ip address dhcp configures that interface as a DHCP client.

questions.stem: Clients can reach their gateway, but new leases fail after the DHCP server moves to another subnet. What should you verify?
options: DHCP relay target and reachability to the server
The OSPF process ID on clients
STP priority on the DNS server
questions.explanation: A correct relay path must reach the server and permit the return traffic.

questions.stem: What is DNS primarily used for?
options: Resolving names to resource records such as IP addresses
questions.explanation: DNS maps names to records. Address assignment is typically DHCP's role.

questions.stem: A website works by IP but fails by hostname. What is a strong next check?
options: DNS resolution and configured DNS servers
questions.explanation: IP reachability with name-only failure points toward name resolution, though application hosting behavior can also matter.

questions.stem: Which DNS record maps a hostname to an IPv6 address?
questions.explanation: AAAA records hold IPv6 addresses; A records hold IPv4 addresses.

questions.stem: Does DNS use only UDP?
options: No; DNS can use both UDP and TCP
questions.explanation: DNS commonly uses UDP for queries but also uses TCP, including for situations requiring reliable larger transfers.

questions.stem: What does NTP synchronize?
questions.explanation: Consistent time supports log correlation and other operations that depend on timestamps.

questions.stem: Which command makes this device an NTP client of 192.0.2.10?
questions.explanation: The ntp server command specifies an upstream time source.

questions.stem: A client synchronizes to a stratum-2 server. What stratum does the client normally advertise?
questions.explanation: NTP stratum increases by one at each synchronization level away from the reference clock.

questions.stem: What does the leading asterisk usually mark in show ntp associations?
questions.explanation: The association marker identifies the peer currently selected for synchronization.

questions.stem: What is the role of an SNMP manager?
options: Collect and manage information from agents
questions.explanation: Management software polls or receives notifications from SNMP agents on managed devices.

questions.stem: What is an SNMP trap?
questions.explanation: Traps notify the manager of events without waiting for a polling request; traditional traps are unacknowledged.

questions.stem: Which SNMPv3 security level provides authentication and encryption?
questions.explanation: authPriv combines authentication and privacy. Merely selecting SNMPv3 does not guarantee encryption without the security level.

questions.stem: What is the severity number in this syslog message?
questions.explanation: The numeric field after the facility is severity. Here LINK is the facility and UPDOWN is the mnemonic.
questions.cli: %LINK-3-UPDOWN: Interface GigabitEthernet0/1, changed state to down

questions.stem: Which syslog level is most severe?
questions.explanation: Syslog severity increases in importance as the number decreases toward zero.

questions.stem: With logging trap warnings, which severity numbers are sent to the syslog server?
questions.explanation: A threshold of warnings (4) includes that level and all more-severe, lower-numbered levels.

questions.stem: Logs from two routers describe the same event several minutes apart. Which service should you verify?
questions.explanation: Unsynchronized clocks make cross-device timelines unreliable.

questions.stem: What does QoS classification do?
questions.explanation: Classification groups traffic according to fields or application information so a policy can act on it.

questions.stem: What does QoS marking do?
options: Set a field such as DSCP to signal treatment
questions.explanation: Marking carries a classification indication that downstream policies may use.

questions.stem: What is a typical difference between shaping and policing?
options: Shaping buffers excess traffic; policing can drop or remark it
questions.explanation: Shaping smooths transmission by queueing. Policing enforces a rate with configured actions on excess traffic.

questions.stem: Why give voice preferential queue treatment under congestion?
options: Voice is sensitive to delay and jitter
questions.explanation: Queue scheduling can reduce waiting for latency-sensitive packets, within available capacity.

questions.stem: What is congestion in an output queue context?
options: Traffic arrives faster than the egress can transmit for a period
An interface has no IP address
questions.explanation: Packets accumulate when demand exceeds service rate; sustained excess can cause drops.

questions.stem: What is the usual TCP port for SSH?
questions.explanation: SSH normally uses TCP 22. Telnet uses 23, while TFTP and SNMP commonly use UDP ports.

questions.stem: Which VTY command restricts incoming remote CLI transport to SSH?
questions.explanation: transport input controls allowed protocols. Authentication settings are also required.

questions.stem: Which file-transfer protocol uses UDP and has no built-in user authentication?
questions.explanation: TFTP is a minimal transfer protocol. Its simplicity comes without built-in authentication or encryption.

questions.stem: How does conventional FTP differ from TFTP?
options: FTP uses TCP and separate control/data connections
questions.explanation: FTP has a TCP control channel and data channel; ordinary FTP is not automatically encrypted.

questions.stem: SSH reaches a router but login fails. What should be inspected after transport connectivity is confirmed?
options: Configured user authentication and VTY login method
questions.explanation: An established connection and successful user authentication are separate steps.

questions.stem: Which security property prevents unauthorized disclosure of information?
questions.explanation: Confidentiality limits exposure; integrity protects correctness and availability concerns access to services.

questions.stem: Which property is primarily affected by unauthorized alteration of configuration?
questions.explanation: Tampering changes the correctness or trustworthiness of data or configuration.

questions.stem: A flood exhausts a server and stops legitimate access. Which property is directly affected?
questions.explanation: A denial-of-service condition prevents authorized users from obtaining service.

questions.stem: What is a vulnerability?
options: A weakness that could be exploited
questions.explanation: A vulnerability is the exploitable weakness; a threat is a potential cause of harm.

questions.stem: Which is an example of social engineering?
options: Impersonating IT support to solicit a password
questions.explanation: Social engineering manipulates people rather than relying solely on a technical exploit.

questions.stem: Which two controls can reduce user credential risk?
questions.explanation: MFA reduces reliance on one factor, while training helps users recognize deceptive requests.

questions.stem: Which two actions follow least privilege?
options: Grant a role only the permissions it needs
Remove access that is no longer required
Share one privileged account across all staff
questions.explanation: Least privilege limits permissions to current needs, reducing the impact of misuse or a compromised account.

questions.stem: Which is a physical security control?
options: Restricted access to network equipment rooms
questions.explanation: Locks and controlled entry protect physical infrastructure; logical controls address other layers.

questions.stem: Which AAA function verifies who a user is?
questions.explanation: Authentication checks identity; authorization determines allowed actions and accounting records activity.

questions.stem: Which AAA function decides whether a user can run a privileged command?
questions.explanation: Permissions are an authorization decision after or alongside identity verification.

questions.stem: Which AAA function records session actions for auditing?
questions.explanation: Accounting provides records such as session times or command activity, depending on configuration.

questions.stem: Which protocol is commonly used for granular device-administration AAA and uses TCP 49?
questions.explanation: TACACS+ commonly supports separate authentication, authorization and accounting services for device administration.

questions.stem: Which protocol is commonly used for 802.1X backend authentication?
questions.explanation: A switch or wireless authenticator commonly exchanges AAA messages with a RADIUS server.

questions.stem: Why is enable secret preferred over legacy enable password?
options: It stores a one-way password representation using the supported secret algorithm
It eliminates the need for AAA
questions.explanation: Secrets avoid legacy cleartext-style password storage; supported algorithms vary by software version.

questions.stem: Does service password-encryption provide strong protection for legacy Type 7 passwords?
options: Yes; it is equivalent to modern password hashing
Yes; it encrypts all SSH keys
questions.explanation: Type 7 is easily reversible and should not be treated as strong cryptographic password storage.

questions.stem: What does login local on VTY lines select?
options: The local username database for login authentication
Only the enable password for every user
questions.explanation: Local user credentials are checked. SSH transport settings and keys are separate prerequisites.

questions.stem: What does a standard IPv4 ACL primarily match?
questions.explanation: Standard ACLs match source addresses; extended ACLs can express more detailed packet criteria.

questions.stem: Which two fields can an extended IPv4 ACL examine?
questions.explanation: Extended ACLs can match protocol and IP addresses and, where appropriate, transport ports.

questions.stem: What happens when a packet matches an ACL entry?
options: That entry's action is used and evaluation stops
Every later rule also overrides it
The router sorts rules by prefix length first
questions.explanation: ACLs are processed in order; the first matching entry decides the action.

questions.stem: What happens to unmatched traffic at the end of an ordinary IPv4 interface ACL?
options: It is denied by the implicit deny
questions.explanation: A permit must match for traffic to pass an applied filtering ACL.

questions.stem: Where are extended ACLs generally placed when practical?
questions.explanation: Filtering unwanted traffic near its source avoids carrying it unnecessarily. Actual placement depends on the policy and topology.

questions.stem: Why are standard ACLs often placed near the destination?
options: They cannot distinguish destinations and could block too broadly near the source
questions.explanation: Source-only matching can affect unrelated destinations if placed too early in the path.

questions.stem: What does this ACL line allow?
options: TCP from any source to HTTPS on 192.0.2.10
questions.explanation: The eq 443 appears after the destination, so it matches the destination port.
questions.cli: permit tcp any host 192.0.2.10 eq 443

questions.stem: Which wildcard matches exactly one IPv4 host?
questions.explanation: Zero wildcard bits must match. The host keyword is shorthand for an exact address match.

questions.stem: What is the wildcard corresponding to 255.255.255.192?
questions.explanation: Invert each mask bit, equivalently subtract each octet from 255.

questions.stem: A deny rule is appended below permit ip any any. Why does the deny never match?
options: The earlier permit already matches the packets
The ACL must use only UDP
questions.explanation: Rule ordering matters. A broad permit shadows later denies for matching traffic.

questions.stem: What does ip access-group FILTER in apply to?
questions.explanation: Direction is relative to the router interface, not the user's idea of inside or outside.

questions.stem: A correct ACL exists but interface traffic is unaffected. What should you verify?
options: That it is applied on the intended interface and direction
That the router hostname matches the ACL name
That every host has static DNS
That the ACL number is the VLAN ID
questions.explanation: An ACL definition does not automatically filter traffic until referenced by an appropriate feature.

questions.stem: What does switch port security restrict?
options: Allowed source MAC addresses on a port
questions.explanation: Port security constrains source MAC use; it is not equivalent to user identity authentication.

questions.stem: What is the default port-security violation action on typical Cisco access switches?
questions.explanation: Shutdown puts the interface into an error-disabled state after a violation.

questions.stem: Which violation mode drops violating traffic and increments a violation counter without shutting the port?
questions.explanation: Restrict drops offending frames and provides notification/counter behavior while the port remains operational.

questions.stem: What does sticky MAC learning do?
options: Adds learned secure MACs to running configuration
Automatically saves every change to startup configuration
questions.explanation: Sticky entries become configuration lines. Persistence across reboot requires saving the configuration.

questions.stem: A port permits one secure MAC but must support a phone and attached PC. What should you verify?
options: Appropriate secure-MAC limits and voice/data design
That both devices share an IP
That all security is disabled globally
That the PC is the STP root
questions.explanation: Two legitimate devices can exceed a one-address policy. Set limits consistent with the intended endpoint arrangement.

questions.stem: What does DHCP snooping help block?
options: Rogue DHCP server messages on untrusted ports
questions.explanation: Snooping distinguishes trusted server-facing paths from untrusted client-facing paths.

questions.stem: Which DHCP snooping port should normally be trusted?
options: The legitimate DHCP server-facing or authorized upstream port
questions.explanation: Trust is assigned where authorized server responses should arrive, not indiscriminately to endpoints.

questions.stem: What does Dynamic ARP Inspection validate?
options: ARP sender bindings against trusted information
questions.explanation: DAI checks ARP validity using information such as DHCP snooping bindings and configured ARP ACLs.

questions.stem: A static-IP host is blocked by DAI because no DHCP binding exists. What is an appropriate solution to evaluate?
options: A correct static binding/ARP ACL or supported policy for that host
questions.explanation: Static hosts need legitimate validation information; the exact supported method depends on platform and policy.

questions.stem: What is a site-to-site VPN commonly used for?
options: Protecting traffic between networks over an untrusted transport
questions.explanation: The tunnel secures intersite traffic while each site's routing and access policy remain necessary.

questions.stem: What distinguishes a remote-access VPN use case?
options: An individual user's device connects securely to an organizational network
Only two fixed branch gateways connect
questions.explanation: Remote access extends protected connectivity to a user's device, often with user authentication.

questions.stem: Which legacy wireless security mechanism is considered insecure?
options: 802.1X with a properly configured secure EAP method
questions.explanation: WEP has fundamental weaknesses and should not be selected for a secure modern WLAN.

questions.stem: How does WPA2-Enterprise typically authenticate users?
options: One universal shared passphrase for every user
questions.explanation: Enterprise authentication supports individual credentials and backend policy, commonly through RADIUS.

questions.stem: Which mechanism is associated with WPA3-Personal authentication?
questions.explanation: Simultaneous Authentication of Equals replaces the older personal-mode PSK handshake approach.

questions.stem: Does hiding an SSID provide strong access protection?
options: No; use proper authentication and encryption
Only if the SSID is short
questions.explanation: The network can still be discovered through wireless activity. Suppressing the name is not a security boundary.

questions.stem: A client associates but enterprise authentication fails. Which two items should be checked?
options: STP root priority on the laptop
questions.explanation: 802.1X success depends on compatible client/server authentication and functioning AAA communication.

questions.stem: Why combine technical controls, user training and physical protections?
options: Different controls address different failure and attack paths
questions.explanation: Layered defenses reduce dependence on any single protective mechanism.

questions.stem: Which two statements about network automation are correct?
options: An incorrect template can spread errors rapidly
questions.explanation: Automation scales both correct behavior and mistakes. Validate inputs and outcomes before expanding a rollout.

questions.stem: Why test an automation workflow on a small scope before broad rollout?
options: To detect errors before they affect many devices
To make the API use UDP
To remove the need for backups
questions.explanation: Small initial scope and verification limit the impact of an incorrect change.

questions.stem: Which plane normally forwards user packets?
questions.explanation: The data plane performs forwarding using information installed by control processes.

questions.stem: Which plane builds routing and topology decisions?
questions.explanation: Routing protocols and topology calculations belong to control-plane functions.

questions.stem: What does a logically centralized controller provide?
options: A coordinated control and policy view across managed devices
A guarantee that every packet passes through its CPU
questions.explanation: Logical centralization concerns control. The controller service may itself be distributed or redundant.

questions.stem: A northbound API typically connects which components?
options: A controller and only its physical switches
A host and its default gateway via ARP
questions.explanation: Northbound interfaces expose controller services to applications or orchestration systems.

questions.stem: A southbound interface typically connects which components?
options: A browser and a public DNS resolver
A hypervisor and its power supply
questions.explanation: Southbound communication conveys control or management information toward network devices.

questions.stem: What is an underlay network?
options: The transport infrastructure providing reachability for an overlay
A replacement for all IP addressing
questions.explanation: The underlay carries encapsulated traffic between overlay endpoints.

questions.stem: What is an overlay network?
options: A logical network built over an underlying transport
questions.explanation: Tunnels and encapsulation can create logical connectivity independent of some physical details.

questions.stem: Why separate policy intent from individual device CLI commands?
options: To express desired outcomes that a system can translate into device configuration
To eliminate the need for verification
To force every device to use one vendor syntax
questions.explanation: Controller-based management can translate policy into implementation while operators still validate outcomes.

questions.stem: Which HTTP method normally retrieves a resource without requesting a modification?
questions.explanation: GET requests a representation. A well-designed API does not use it to perform state-changing actions.

questions.stem: Which HTTP method commonly creates a resource under a collection?
questions.explanation: POST commonly submits data to create a new subordinate resource, subject to the API contract.

questions.stem: Which HTTP method commonly replaces the representation at a known resource URI?
questions.explanation: PUT requests creation or replacement at the target URI; replacement behavior depends on the API schema.

questions.stem: Which HTTP method commonly makes a partial resource update?
questions.explanation: PATCH applies a partial modification instead of replacing the entire representation.

questions.stem: Which HTTP method normally requests removal of a resource?
questions.explanation: DELETE expresses resource removal; permissions and the endpoint's contract control the outcome.

questions.stem: What does statelessness mean for REST requests?
options: Each request supplies the context needed to process it
The server stores no resources at all
Every request must use the same TCP connection
questions.explanation: Stateless request handling does not prohibit databases. It avoids reliance on server-held client session context between requests.

questions.stem: An API returns HTTP 401. What should you inspect first?
questions.explanation: 401 indicates an authentication problem or missing authentication. Authorization failures commonly use 403.

questions.stem: An authenticated API call returns HTTP 403. What is the likely category of failure?
options: Permission to perform the requested operation
questions.explanation: 403 commonly means access is forbidden despite the request being understood; inspect policy and authorization.

questions.stem: What does a 404 response commonly mean?
options: The requested resource was not found
The response is a DNS reply
questions.explanation: Check the URI and resource identifier; a 404 is an HTTP response rather than a transport timeout.

questions.stem: What does HTTP 201 commonly indicate?
options: A resource was deleted with no content
questions.explanation: 201 Created indicates successful creation; the response may identify the new resource.

questions.stem: Why protect a bearer token in an API request?
options: Possession can allow use of its granted permissions
questions.explanation: Treat tokens as credentials, restrict their scope and avoid exposing them in logs or source code.

questions.stem: Which two protections can correctly configured HTTPS provide for an API?
options: Integrity protection for traffic in transit
questions.explanation: TLS protects the transport. Authentication, authorization and application validation still have separate jobs.

questions.stem: Which content type identifies a JSON body?
questions.explanation: Content-Type describes the representation being sent; Accept can indicate the desired response representation.

questions.stem: Which delimiters enclose a JSON object?
questions.explanation: Objects contain name/value pairs; arrays use square brackets.

questions.stem: Which delimiters enclose a JSON array?
questions.explanation: An array is an ordered sequence of JSON values.

questions.stem: Which value is a JSON boolean?
questions.explanation: JSON booleans are unquoted lowercase true or false. Quoted text is a string.

questions.stem: What is the type of the value assigned to interfaces?
questions.explanation: Square brackets indicate an array containing two strings.
questions.cli: {"interfaces":["Gi0/0","Gi0/1"]}

questions.stem: Why is this not valid JSON?
options: The key uses single quotes instead of double quotes
questions.explanation: JSON member names must be double-quoted strings; true is already valid.
questions.cli: {'enabled': true}

questions.stem: What value is stored at device.name?
questions.explanation: The outer object's device member is another object whose name member is the string R1.
questions.cli: {"device":{"name":"R1","sshPort":22}}

questions.stem: What is wrong with this JSON?
options: A trailing comma follows the last object member
The number needs to be quoted
Objects must contain at least two keys
questions.explanation: Standard JSON does not allow trailing commas.

questions.stem: What is an Ansible playbook typically used to describe?

questions.stem: What is Terraform commonly used for?
questions.explanation: Terraform describes desired resources and uses providers to interact with platforms.

questions.stem: What does idempotence mean in configuration management?
options: Repeating the desired-state operation should not keep making unnecessary changes

questions.stem: A manually changed device differs from its intended configuration. What is this often called?
questions.explanation: Drift is divergence between actual and desired state; automation can help detect and reconcile it.

questions.stem: Which task best illustrates predictive AI in network operations?
options: Forecasting capacity demand from historical usage
Assigning a static VLAN by hand
questions.explanation: Predictive methods estimate future values or outcomes using patterns in data.

questions.stem: Which task best illustrates generative AI assistance?
options: Drafting an explanation or configuration proposal from a prompt
Merely forwarding a packet by its destination MAC
questions.explanation: Generative systems produce content. Their proposals still need technical review and testing.

questions.stem: Why validate an AI-generated network configuration before deployment?
options: It can contain plausible but incorrect or unsupported commands
questions.explanation: Generated output may omit context or invent syntax. Check platform documentation and test behavior.

questions.stem: How can machine learning help detect network anomalies?
options: Learn patterns and identify departures from expected behavior
questions.explanation: Anomaly detection highlights unusual patterns; investigation determines whether they indicate incidents or legitimate changes.
